Similar to agentic vision , which combines code execution with Gemini models’ native image understanding, agentic video understanding uses Gemini’s native video tools to improve performance and unlock new capabilities for video processing like sub-second moment retrieval, more accurate anomaly detection, precise counting and more. The feature is available today for video uploads and YouTube videos via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Across standard video analysis benchmarks, Gemini models with agentic video understanding reduce analysis costs by up to 66% and token consumption by up to 88%, while improving accuracy by up to 7%. These efficiency gains are especially pronounced on long-form video (from 10-minute how-to guides to 90-minute lectures and multi-hour recordings), where static processing forces developers to choose between high token costs or techniques that drop critical details.

items.full_text_snippet: Building trust in proprietary model benchmarks using cryptographically secure environments Imagine a student is set to take a high-stakes exam. If they accidentally peek at the test questions in advance, achieving a perfect score is influenced by this knowledge, making it a meaningless accomplishment. To truly measure what they know, they must have no visibility of the test questions until it's time to take the exam. That is the exact challenge the industry faces when evaluating advanced AI models. items.full_text_snippet:
GITHUB HUGGING FACE MODELSCOPE DISCORD Background # The Mixture-of-Experts (MoEs) architecture has become a popular model-parameter-scale-up technique. Typically, one MoE layer consists of a router (often parameterized as one single Linear layer) and a group of experts (for transformer-based models, each expert is one feedforward layer). Given an input, only a subset of experts will be activated, and then their outputs will be aggregated based on the scores the router assigned. Specifically, $$
\mathbb{y}=\sum_{i\in N_E,g_i\in\operatorname{topK}}g_i(\mathbb{x})E_i(\mathbb{x})
$$ Load Balancing loss # Load balancing loss is an essential regularization technique in training MoE-based networks, and high-level intuition encourages the balanced activation of all experts. It can be calculated as: $$
L_{\text{balance}}=N_E \sum_{i=1}^{N_E} f_ip_i
$$ where $f_i$ is the activation frequency of the expert $E_i$, and the $p_i$ is the the average gating score that the expert $E_i$ is assigned. However, most existing MoE training frameworks (e.g., Megatron-core), implement micro-batch level balance, which means the $L_{\text{balance}}$ is calculated within every micro-batch and is then averaged on the global batch level. Our key point is that this implementation could be problematic if one micro-batch does not contain diverse data. For instance, imagine one micro-batch only contains some code data; the aforementioned load-balancing loss still pushes the router to distribute these code tokens to all experts uniformly, potentially hurting the model performance and preventing expert specialization. This situation is even more common in training MoE-based LLMs: the data in one micro-batch is often from the same domain. This partially explains why most existing open-source MoE-based LLMs do not achieve notable expert specialization. items.full_text_snippet: Multimodal agents commonly generate freeform reasoning before each action. For small models, limited model capacity can result in lengthy reasoning that provides little useful guidance for action generation while incurring substantial inference cost. To address this challenge, we introduce Selection-based Structured Reasoning (SSR), a framework that reformulates reasoning as selection instead of open-ended generation. SSR represents recurring high-level reasoning as pre-specified, reusable natural-language candidates. At each turn, the model selects from the reasoning candidates based on their likelihoods given the current context, without an auxiliary task head. Using pre-specified reasoning traces enables parallel scoring, where teacher-forced prefilling computes token likelihoods concurrently within and across candidates using a shared context KV cache. We evaluated SSR on seven multimodal search benchmarks using 2B and 4B models. Across multiple reinforcement learning objectives and supervised fine-tuning, SSR delivers significant efficiency gains without sacrificing task performance. SSR achieves an average success rate competitive with leading search agents of the same scale, while reducing per-turn reasoning latency by over 90% and total per-question model inference latency by 28–54%. † Carnegie Mellon University ‡ University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign ** Work partially done while at Apple *** Work done while at Apple

A rank-1 adapter is a few megabytes, so it can travel through a Storage Bucket mounted in every Job instead of over NCCL. The trainer and the vLLM replicas run as separate Hugging Face Jobs on separate machines. A small proxy in front of the replicas adds the auth header, routes each rollout to the replica that already holds its KV prefix, and broadcasts adapter loads to every replica. The AsyncGRPO metrics show where the bottleneck sits. Five runs take the same recipe from 3 h 27 min to 53 min for 500 steps. LoRA support recently landed in TRL's AsyncGRPOTrainer with PR #7017 , and ships with TRL v1.14. The asynchronous trainer can now train an adapter instead of the full model, and it syncs only the LoRA adapter to vLLM. items.full_text_snippet: Elorian , the Palo Alto AI startup that raised a $55 million seed round at a $300 million valuation before it launched a product, released its first model on Friday, TechCrunch has exclusively learned. The model, Glimpse , is launching as a research preview with API access and a chat interface is waitlist-only, so for now it’s a results table and a thesis. The thesis? Today’s AI models, for all their skill with language and code, still can’t really see. Most multimodal models look at an image once, convert it to tokens, and then reason about it in text — like describing a photo from memory. Glimpse keeps going back to the source. Mid-reasoning, it can crop into a region, pull specific frames from a video, or run code to measure or compare what it’s looking at, a mechanism Elorian calls a “visual scratch space.” Think of someone pinching to zoom on a phone photo to double-check what they thought they saw. For former Google DeepMind researcher and Elorian CEO Andrew Dai, one of the clearest signs that AI still couldn’t really see came on game night. Last year he photographed a board game he’d just finished with friends and asked a frontier model who was winning. It couldn’t say. Board games “each have their own visual language, each have their own iconography, symbols,” he told TechCrunch. “To an adult, it’s quite easy to understand what’s going on with minimal text, but these models aren’t able to intuit what the symbols mean.” “Humans can look at Ikea diagrams, with no text, and assemble Ikea furniture, right? Why can’t AI models?” he said. The approach isn’t completely new — OpenAI added crop-and-zoom during reasoning to its o-series models in 2025 — but Elorian’s pitch is that it built the whole model around it, cheaply. items.full_text_snippet: Jev has become the fastest adopted AI model ever — at least by some measures. Vercel data published on Thursday shows that, within two weeks of its launch, the buzzy decision model was being used by 35% of paid teams, with nearly double the reach of the second most popular model, Sonnet 5.5. It’s the fastest adoption a model has ever seen in its first two weeks, according to Vercel’s data, and a major accomplishment for the model’s creators, TypeSafe AI. Published in limited release on September 15, Jev is designed as a lightweight tool for choosing between a few predetermined outputs. Limiting the outputs lets the model run cheaper and faster than alternatives like Sonnet, making it ideal for classifying large quantities of data quickly. That new approach has attracted significant buzz in the weeks since Jev’s release — inspiring competing offerings from OpenAI and Amazon , among others — but until now there has been little hard data to back up the good vibes. The data comes from Vercel’s AI gateway , a unified API service similar to OpenRouter. It’s a necessarily limited view — particularly at risk of undercounting major labs like OpenAI and Anthropic that offer their own APIs — but it shows the buzz around Jev really did translate into actual usage. In fact, Vercel was an early adopter of Jev, using it to replace GPT-6 Luna for classifying harmful commands. The report also shows continuing momentum for open source models, which now account for more than 70% of the tokens processed through Vercel’s gateway and nearly 25% of the total spend. While open source models are capturing a larger share of the market, the market is also growing fast. Spending on frontier labs has grown tenfold, even as it accounts for a smaller share of overall spend, giving credence to the idea that frontier models and open source alternatives may turn out to be complementary rather than competitive .

Monte Carlo simulations (or methods ) is the technique of applying
randomness and the Law of large numbers to the solution of various scientific and engineering problems. One of its
first documented uses was by Stanislaw Ulam and John von Neumann for nuclear
weapon simulations after WWII . In this post I want to provide examples of some simple uses of Monte Carlo
simulations. We'll start with the classical example of calculating the value
of \pi by throwing darts. Estimating pi Suppose we take a square board and inscribe a quarter of a circle into it. We
then proceed to throw darts at the board and record whether each dart hits
inside or outside the quarter circle. Having thrown many such darts, we
calculate the ratio of the darts inside the circle to the total number thrown. Assuming our darts are distributed uniformly over the
square, by the Law of large numbers this ratio should approach the ratio of
areas of the quarter circle A_{circ} to the full square A_{square} . With a square side length of 1, we have: \[\frac{A_{circ}}{A_{square}}=\frac{\pi/4}{1}=\frac{\pi}{4}\] Therefore: \[\pi\approx 4\frac{\text{hits inside}}{\text{total throws}}\] Here's a visualization: A quarter circle of radius 1 inside a unit square. Change the number of samples (dart throws) and click "Run" to regenerate. The

items.full_text_snippet: 钢化膜和手机壳是我们比较常用的两类手机配件，最近我们也上架了厚度为 0.17mm 的升级版麦金獭钢化膜，并且这段时间，我大多都搭配着极稚为 iPhone 18 系列推出的新款墨水屏手机壳使用。前者关注每天都要接触的屏幕，后者则通过可以更换图案的电子墨水屏，让手机背面有了更多变化。 经过十几天的体验，这篇文章想从正面的手感与显示聊起，再翻到背面看看换图的玩法。 正面体验：厚度、热弯与日常触感 升级版麦金獭钢化膜从初代的 0.13mm 增加到 0.17mm，在保持轻薄手感的同时，兼顾日常使用中的耐久性，并且通过了德国 TÜV 莱茵认证。测试涵盖雾度、透光率、环境对比度等显示指标，以及高低温、75% 酒精擦拭、钢丝绒摩擦和人工皮肤刮擦等耐久性项目。经过相关测试后，产品的总反射率衰减比例仍保持在 50% 以上。 参数之外，日常操作中更容易感受到的是边缘处理。这些年 iPhone 的交互越来越依赖边缘手势，返回、切换 App、呼出控制中心、回到桌面，许多高频操作都会经过屏幕边缘。近几代 iPhone 的屏幕边缘也都带有一定的微曲面过渡。如果钢化膜无法很好地贴合这部分区域，就容易出现覆盖不完整、边缘割手感明显等问题。 和初代一样，升级版麦金獭钢化膜依然采用了 3D 热弯工艺，能够更好地贴合 iPhone 屏幕边缘的微曲面，实现更完整的覆盖效果，让玻璃边缘与屏幕之间的过渡更加自然。 左：无热弯钢化膜；右：麦金獭钢化膜 相比初代 0.13mm 的厚度，升级版增加到 0.17mm 后，边缘的存在感难免更强一点，好在这点厚度的增加对日常滑动手势的影响并不明显，自然的边缘贴合保证了手指经过边缘时的顺畅体验，无论是从屏幕左右两侧滑动返回、从底部上滑切换应用，还是连续刷信息流、来回切换应用，都没有明显的硌手感。 升级版麦金獭 AR 钢化膜延续了初代的磁控溅射工艺，平均透光率达到 96%。平时办公室光线比较稳定时，看文档、回消息、浏览网页，都能保证屏幕显示清晰，和高清钢化膜相比差异并不明显；到了户外，这种区别更容易感受到，阳光比较强的时候，屏幕难免会有反光，但画面内容受环境光的影响相对小一些，路线和文字也比较容易看清。 相比透光率、反光率这些更容易被量化的参数，日常触感还有一些需要持续使用才能留意到的细节。比如平时通勤刷信息流、回复消息、看视频，肯定会在屏幕上留下一些指纹，但搭配升级版麦金獭 AR 钢化膜这些指纹残留并不会太明显，纸巾一擦就干净了。天气热、手指出汗的时候，滑动屏幕也没有生硬的拖拽感。 背面表达：让背面多一块能换图案的屏 换一张图片就能改变手机背面的样子，这是极稚墨水屏手机壳和普通手机壳不一样的地方。背面的电子墨水屏可以自由更换图案，手机壳也不再只有一个固定的外观。 这块墨水屏的分辨率为 400×400 像素，212 DPI 与入门款墨水屏阅读器类似，显示效果相当不错，足够应对各类图片素材。投屏速度相比上一代也有提升，最快约 20 秒就能完成一次投屏。 除了图案，壳体本身也提供月岩白、深空灰、海盐蓝、浆果红和史莱姆绿五种配色。这一代还新增了挂绳片卡槽，并附赠专属挂绳片，让日常携带多了一种选择。 背部的凸起磁吸结构设计保留了 MagSafe 兼容性，能正常搭配 MagSafe 生态配件，也不干扰无线充电。和之前的款式相比，这一代的变化更多在换图速度、配色和携带方式这些细节上。 壳膜之间的边缘空间 升级版麦金獭钢化膜拥有较高的屏幕覆盖率，能够更完整地贴合屏幕边缘，减少裸露区域，让视觉和触感上的过渡更加自然。但膜覆盖得越完整，留给手机壳边缘的空间就越少，对手机壳的边缘设计与尺寸精度也提出了更高的要求。 虽然换成其他包裹范围较大的全包手机壳时，偶尔能感觉到手机壳边缘与钢化膜之间存在轻微挤压。实际搭配下来，极稚墨水屏手机壳在边缘空间控制上较为精准，既保留了对手机边框的充分包裹，又为钢化膜预留了恰到好处的空间。经过多次拆装，也没有出现顶膜或翘边的情况。 如果你如果平时习惯搭配全包壳，还是需要多留意一下边缘空间。 一部手机的两面体验 如果你正在挑选钢化膜，仍然可以按常用场景来选：平时主要在室内使用，高清版就能满足日常需求；经常通勤、户外拍照或查看导航，更在意强光下的屏幕可读性，可以考虑 AR 款。升级版 0.17mm 麦金獭钢化膜目前适配以下机型： iPhone 18 Pro / 18 Pro Max iPhone 17 / 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max iPhone Air 这次搭配的极稚墨水屏手机壳主要是面向 iPhone 18 系列。如果在日常保护之外，还希望手机背面能随自己的喜好变化，可以从喜欢的配色和图案进行选购。

items.full_text_snippet: 📄 Tech Report: http://allenai.org/papers/benchmirt | 📊 Data: https://huggingface.co/collections/allenai/benchmirt | 💻 Code: https://github.com/allenai/BenchMIRT Today we’re introducing BenchMIRT, a new method for auditing LLM benchmarks at the level of individual prompts—the questions and tasks a model is scored on. A benchmark is usually designed to measure a particular ability, such as safety, general reasoning, or instruction following. But the individual tasks inside it may depend on more than that stated goal. Take BBQ, a benchmark designed to test whether models rely on social stereotypes. One question asks about a grandson and grandfather trying to book an Uber. It probes age bias, but also requires the model to track who’s who and reason from the evidence provided rather than assumptions. And even within a single benchmark, different groups of questions and tasks can measure different things. WildJailbreak, for example, includes harmful jailbreak prompts alongside benign prompts designed to test whether a model refuses harmless requests too often. The harmful prompts are more closely associated with safety, while the benign prompts are more closely associated with general reasoning. Averaging them into a single benchmark score can obscure that difference. BenchMIRT helps researchers separate those signals and see what’s actually driving a benchmark’s score. It does this by analyzing how models perform on each question or task and estimating which underlying capabilities are most closely associated with getting it right. Finding the signals inside a benchmark BenchMIRT takes cues from Item Response Theory (IRT), a technique originating in psychometrics—the field concerned with measuring abilities and traits from patterns of test responses. IRT starts from a simple idea: not every question tells you the same amount about the person taking a test. items.full_text_snippet: Counterfeits of luxury goods are a major problem for fashion houses. Counterfeiters are getting better at replicating brands’ marks and passing off dupes, known as “ superfakes ,” as genuine items. A startup called Veritas wants to tackle the problem with its own chip that verifies goods. Veritas was founded by Luci Holland, a former Tesla technical product manager who also has a background in design and art. Its chip is built to be easily inserted into products without damaging them. Brands can use it to verify whether a product is the real deal, and customers can show a certificate of ownership through the company’s app. Holland said other approaches are easier to defeat, because a digital record can be reproduced through a copied QR code or static NFC link. “Our approach combines secure, authenticated chip responses with integration into the product itself. Our chip generates a secure response with each tap and includes a tamper-detection wire. We make the connection between the object and its digital identity part of the proof,” Holland said. The Veritas founder told TechCrunch over email that the company has just introduced the second version of its chip, which works on metal surfaces and can be scanned through glass. “The next-generation chip is ready for production and supports a broader range of applications, including jewelry, trophies, hard-surface products, and glass objects such as fragrance bottles,” Holland said. “Alongside our garment integrations, this gives brands more ways to incorporate authentication directly into their products.” This week, the startup announced a partnership with ATHLOS, a women’s track-and-field competition founded by Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian, who is also an investor in Veritas. As part of the partnership, all 18 championship crowns will include Veritas’ chips so they can be verified. items.full_text_snippet: I love software rendering. The best DOS experience I’ve had in a long while was Quake in its software renderer at 800×600, running at a locked 60fps on my Dell OptiPlex 380 . It’s one of the best-looking things I’ve seen a DOS game do. That’s not how most people remember those games looking. In the 90s you either ran them in software at a low resolution, or you bought a 3D card and played the accelerated version. Today there’s a third option: run the software renderer on a machine fast enough to push it at resolutions nobody could use back then. What software rendering is In a software-rendered game, the CPU draws every pixel. There’s no 3D card involved: the game works out each frame in its own code and writes it straight to video memory. Doom, Duke Nukem 3D, Blood and the original Quake all work this way. When 3D cards arrived, many games got accelerated versions. GLQuake came after Quake, and Blood and Tomb Raider got 3dfx modes. Those versions hand the drawing to the graphics card, and they look different. Why I like the look It’s sharp. Software renderers generally sample textures pixel by pixel, so every texel stays a crisp square. Early 3D cards smoothed textures with bilinear filtering, which looked impressive in 1997 but turns everything soft and blurry to my eye now. It’s gritty. Most of these games ran in 256 colours, with lighting done through lookup tables into that palette. Shadows fall off in visible steps rather than smooth gradients. Technically that’s colour banding, a limitation. In practice it gives the games a rough, grimy texture that I really like, and that hardware rendering smooths away. It’s how the games were built. Quake was released with its software renderer, and GLQuake followed. Doom and the Build engine games were designed around their software renderers from the start. It isn’t always the better option. items.full_text_snippet: Our estimates of total economic coverage, and of patterns in coverage, all come from the initial list of 29 benchmarks we chose. This is not a complete or perfectly representative sample of the broader universe of unsaturated, public, agentic economic benchmarks. Any incomplete list will necessarily bias down estimates of economic coverage, and it is difficult to bound that bias. We want to stress, therefore, that these results are provisional. We will update them as we expand the initial benchmark list. We also capped the number of included benchmarks in each job family in order to maximize breadth of coverage. We think this makes our estimate of economy-wide benchmark coverage more accurate, at the cost of biasing down our estimates of coverage in the most-benchmarked job families (e.g. software engineering). By selecting for unsaturated benchmarks, we risk understating benchmark coverage on O*NET tasks which are easier for LLMs to complete. On the other hand, including saturated benchmarks would risk overstating benchmark coverage if saturation is downstream of lower task realism. The latter claim seems likely, given that benchmarks often overstate LLM performance in real-world deployments. We think that the bias from including saturated benchmarks would be greater than the bias from excluding them, but neither option is ideal. Finally, while we outline our benchmark selection criteria in the Benchmark Index tab, several criteria (like “Economic Realism”) are difficult to formalize and introduce some subjectivity in our choices.

items.full_text_snippet: Today, Rep. Ritchie Torres (NY-15) announced he will introduce the Power To The Players Act , legislation that would direct the Federal Trade Commission to establish regulations protecting consumers’ ability to own and play the video games they purchase. Over the past few years, video game companies have moved toward digital-only games and consoles, removing the option to buy or use physical games. These digital games are often sold as revocable licenses rather than owned outright, leaving players dependent on the company’s continued support. NBA 2K25 is a clear example. The game, which retailed for $69.99 for the standard edition and $99.99 for the All-Star Edition, will be delisted from digital storefronts on October 30 and will have its online servers shut down on December 31, only two years after its initial release. No consumer should have a game they paid for pulled out from under them on a company’s arbitrary timeline. “When you pay for a game, you should own it,” said Rep. Torres. “Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy. A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale. Families in the Bronx and across the country save up to buy these games, and they deserve better than a license that can vanish at any time. The Power To The Players Act ensures consumers own what they buy and can keep playing long after a company moves on.” Under the bill, buying a video game would give the consumer ownership of the game rather than a license to play it. Games with online functionality would also be required to provide an offline mode before the servers supporting them are shut down. The legislation aims to close the gap between buying a game and owning it. By preserving consumers’ ability to own and resell their games, the bill would ensure that players can keep playing the games they paid for with friends and family for years to come.

My question turned out to have two answers. Support），一件挂在车手肩膀和头盔之间的碳纤维护具，后面细讲。车都撞得四分五裂了，连碳纤维护具都拉断了，人却活着出了院——平时不怎么看赛车的朋友刷到这类事故视频，最常冒出来的问题大概是： 车都撞成废铁了，人为什么还能活？ 一场「四棒接力」 把米尔罗伊这场事故从撞击到脱困拆开看，现代赛车的保命机制是一场「四棒接力」： 车体先碎，替人卸力 HANS 拉住头颈 Halo 罩住头顶 items.title: 让读书笔记不再吃灰：我做了一款跨平台书摘管理工具
items.summary: 从微信读书的 3 万条划线出发，我做了一个让阅读笔记重新回到日常的 App。 查看全文
items.full_text_snippet: Matrix 首页推荐 Matrix 是少数派的写作社区，我们主张分享真实的产品体验，有实用价值的经验与思考。我们会不定期挑选 Matrix 最优质的文章，展示来自用户的最真实的体验和观点。 文章代表作者个人观点，少数派仅对标题和排版略作修改。 我在微信读书里读了 1200 多个小时，留下了 3 万多条划线和想法。 大多数时候，一本书读完，就接着读下一本。像赶路人一样，不断追赶着读更多的书，却搁置了那些当初被触动、被启发的句子。 所以去年 12 月，我开始独立开发 Booko。起初只是为了整理和回顾我自己的微信读书笔记，让它们重新派上用场。 但是在开发的过程中，我也意识到很多读者并不一定用微信读书，他们可能在 Kindle、Apple 图书、得到，或者是豆瓣阅读上阅读。 于是 Booko 逐渐变成了一个支持多平台导入、集中记录和回顾的读书笔记 App。它在 5 月初正式上线，经过几个月的迭代，目前已经支持 iPhone、iPad、Mac 和 Apple Watch。不管在手机、电脑还是抬起手腕，都能随时看到过去留下的那些句子。 多平台笔记导入 我的大部分阅读在微信读书里完成，所以最先解决的就是它的导入。 Booko 刚上线时，只能在微信读书里手动复制划线，再回到 App 里粘贴。面对几百本书，一本本复制不仅繁琐，也没有封面。 5 月中旬微信读书 Skill 上线后，提供了读取书架、划线和想法的接口，我便第一时间把它接入了 Booko。现在只要填入微信读书 API Key，就能一键批量导入所有书籍和笔记。Booko 应该是第一个接入微信读书 Skill 的产品。 除了微信读书，Booko 也支持导入 Kindle、Apple 图书、豆瓣阅读、得到和掌阅的笔记。不同平台的内容都会按书籍整理在同一个书架里。 导入的内容集中在 Booko 的「库」里。进入后是一面整齐的书籍封面墙，点进任意一本书，页面背景色会根据封面自适应变化。 如果遇到某条来自微信读书的划线需要看上下文，点击回顾页左上角的链接图标，就能直接跳回原书对应的章节继续阅读。 随手记录与合集整理 在读书笔记之外，我也想有一个地方安放零碎的想法。它们未必来自某本书，网页或 PDF 里的精妙段落、散步时突发的灵感，都需要随时记下来。 灵感往往稍纵即逝，为了让记录尽量没有阻碍，Booko 打通了系统级的各个入口： iPhone / iPad ：遇到网页或文章里的段落，通过系统共享面板（Share Sheet）直接存入；也可以在桌面小组件里直接打字，或者用快捷指令自动化记录。 Mac ：选中任何软件里的文字，点击右键菜单就能一键发送到 Booko。 存入时不需要停下来纠结该怎么分类，所有内容都会先进入「收集箱」或默认指定的某本书。记的动作越简单，就越容易坚持下来；至于归类，可以等想整理时再说。 当积累的内容变多、想要整理时，Booko 提供了「合集」。它和内容之间是多对多的关系，就像 Apple Music 的播放列表：一首歌可以属于不同的歌单，一条书摘或想法也可以出现在不同的合集里。 比如建立一个「产品思考」合集，里面既可以放《设计心理学》里的划线，也可以放其他 App 里摘录的段落和随手记下的点子。不必为每条内容指定唯一的分类位置，在不同场景下都能方便地找到。 随机回顾与随处可见 按书查看和随机回顾，是两种完全不同的阅读方式。按书看适合重新梳理某一本书，而随机回顾则不需要先决定今天看什么。在 Booko 的「回顾」页里，可以选择按顺序浏览，也可以切换到随机模式。 切换到随机模式后，下一条内容没有固定的顺序，也不用先挑一本书。只是想看看过去读过什么时，打开回顾页就能开始翻。按顺序看适合连续沉浸，随机看则多了一点不期而遇的期待。 更重要的是，回顾不应该只发生在打开 App 的时候。iPhone、iPad 和 Mac 的桌面小组件会常驻显示一条书摘，不用进入 App 就能看到；每日推送则会在设定的时间发来一条过去的划线。 这次上线的 Apple Watch 版，也会把随机回顾同步到手表，并支持放进表盘。抬腕看时间时，表盘里同时显示一条过去的书摘，让那些沉睡的记录在不经意间重新回到眼前。 重新设计的 Mac 版 很多人把读书笔记 App 默认当成手机应用。但对我来说，每天上班对着 Mac，下班做 Side Project 依然在用 items.full_text_snippet: AI agents from multiple providers accessed personal data and confidential material at Indian organizations during research and testing, India’s cybersecurity agency said Thursday. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received “multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers” whose models, during research and evaluation runs on the open internet, “had reached the live systems of Indian organizations.” The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles, and their actions “exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks.” This makes India the latest stop on what has become a world tour for rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI’s agents escaped a test environment and hacked French company Hugging Face — kicking off a summer of rogue AI agent activity. Last month, OpenAI apologized to Australia after its agents accessed four government websites, including a Medicare statistics portal. At Hugging Face, OpenAI’s agents started the same way but then found and exploited software flaws to run code on the company’s servers. CERT-In described no such hacking in India, where the agents appear to have simply used the access left lying around. Still, the Indian cases appear to be worse in one respect, which is what the agents saw: In Australia, OpenAI said it found no evidence its agents touched individuals’ medical or criminal records, even after they wrote files inside a Medicare statistics system, while in India, agents read personal data and confidential business records. And unlike earlier incidents, each disclosed by a single lab, India’s case involved agents from multiple providers. items.full_text_snippet: “It’s just timestamps”: the decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained. We pursued this long-standing open question of the cryptographic community to settle concerns about ECDSA, which is one of our most widely used cryptographic standards. Readers should take this as a fun closing chapter and the end of years of speculation. There is no action to be taken or things to do differently. Most researchers trusted the curves already. Enjoy. ECDSA is the most widely used elliptic curve cryptography standard. It was adopted by NIST in 2000 as part of the FIPS 186-2 Digital Signature Standard which lists a set of standard elliptic curves of varying sizes and security levels. For curves over prime and binary fields, the specifications published a “seed” parameter whose hash value is used to define the coefficient b of the curve. The provenance of these seeds has been a long-standing question, as they were provided by the NSA with no explanation or justification. As an example, the NIST P-256 curve seed was SEED = C49D3608 86E70493 6A6678E1 139D26B7 819F7E90 with no information where it came from. Neal Koblitz and Alfred Menezes wrote an excellent summary on this controversy, “ A Riddle Wrapped in an Enigma ”, which discusses the history and concerns around the seed values. This mystery led to an amateur investigation into the origin of the seeds and a bounty for anyone who could find them . The best story was that Jerry Solinas, longtime NSA employee, generated the seeds using a hash of a humorous passphrase: “I believe there was a counter rather than multiple hashing, but I don’t know details. The message was along the lines of ‘Give Bob and Jerry a raise’ or ‘Bob and Jerry rule’ or something like that. It was Bob Reiter who actually wrote the code, and he doesn’t remember the details either. Nor were we able to find archives from so long ago. items.full_text_snippet: For the last few days I have been playing with RFC8950 setup, which allows routing of IPv4 on top of IPv6. While logically it’s quite simple, it has a very powerful application towards making “ IPv4 an optional ” feature riding on top of an IPv6 network ( but without any tunnels! ) Some of the interesting use cases: A large network can run IPv6 only everywhere on its core and leave IPv4 only on edge devices. This can work without customers doing any tweaking at their end. They still do things the old way but Backbone can run IPv6 only at its core. An IP transit backbone can run IPv6 only while exchanging IPv4 routes with its customers/peers/upstream over IPv6 sessions. So IPv4 as a “feature” stays but the network in itself is IPv6 only without the overhead of IPv4 interface config, BGP session config, firewall config, etc. An IXP can offer services without IPv4 essentually by using a (unique) IPv6 at the IX LAN & running route server to exchange both IPv4 & IPv6 routes over the IPv6 only session. Thus what 464XLAT did to the mobile networks - this has the potential to do that for the backbone networks. How does it work? Multi-protocol BGP (MP-BGP) supports announcement of IPv4 routes over IPv6 sessions with IPv4 next-hops and IPv6 routes over IPv4 sessions with IPv6 next-hops. RFC8950 extends this feature for IPv4 to have IPv6 next-hops. So for IPv4 address, next hop is IPv6, IPv6 reach works via usual NDP and IPv4 rides on ethernet frames to the same MAC as discovered by the NDP. Technically RFC8950 only impacts control plane decisions by using IPv6 as the control plane but keeps the data plane as it is. IPv4 stays IPv4 & goes as IPv4 over the wire unlike say some tunnel or 464xLAT etc. Hardware support As of now it’s quite widely supported by a lot of routing platforms like Juniper JunOS, Cisco IOS XR, Nokia SR OS, Mikrotik, Huawei, BIRD, FRR etc. So, it is very likely supported if you are running a recent version of the OS.
